subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 grouped GitHub Action revisions in secret-bearing and code-executing workflows after an exact-current-main validation run?
rationale: The diff has no identifiable code defect, but CI cannot decide whether the repository should trust the new upstream action code in token, publishing, scanning, and agent-execution boundaries.

options.title: Refresh, verify, and approve
options.body: Rebase onto current main, verify official release-to-SHA provenance, rerun the affected workflow gates, and approve the grouped update if the exact head is clean.

options.title: Split privileged action families
options.body: Separate Codex, token, Docker publishing, and CodeQL revisions into smaller PRs when owners want independent provenance review or rollback.

options.title: Pause the grouped update
options.body: Leave the PR unmerged until Dependabot access and exact-head checks are stable enough to validate the full bundle.

recommendation.title: Refresh, verify, and approve
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main, verify official release-to-SHA provenance, rerun the affected workflow gates, and approve the grouped update if the exact head is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline directly routes this security-sensitive workflow bundle to steipete through a mention and subscription.
